# Best home backup power stations under $1,000

For most people I'd pick the **Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2** (about $900) if you want the most capacity and room to grow. The **Bluetti AC180** ($499) is the better value if a smaller unit is enough.

## My picks

**1. Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2, best overall (~$899.99)**
- It has 2,048 Wh and 2,400 W output, with a 10 ms UPS switchover.
- You can add a BP2000 battery later to reach 4 kWh. The Bluetti Elite 200 V2 can't expand.
- It runs a fridge for about 1.6 days, per Outage Outfitter.
- Sources: [Outage Authority](https://outageauthority.com/roundups/best-power-station-home-backup), [Outage Outfitter](https://outageoutfitter.com/best/under-1000/). Both pages have the Amazon buy button.

**2. Bluetti AC180, best budget pick ($499)**
- It has 1,152 Wh and 1,800 W output, with a 5-year warranty.
- It covers a fridge for about 22 hours, plus a router and CPAP, or short outages.
- It can't be expanded, and it weighs about 35 lb.
- **[Buy at Bluetti's US store](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180)** (affiliate link; the site earns a commission at no cost to you). Dealectric says code AFF5OFF took $24.95 off, to about $474, when tested in Bluetti's cart on 2026-10-21. Checkout has the final word on price.
- Source: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180)

**3. Bluetti Elite 200 V2, the best battery, if the price is right (~$899)**
- It has 2,074 Wh, 2,600 W output, and a 6,000-cycle LiFePO4 pack. That is roughly double the rated life of the others.
- **Prices conflict.** Compare Power Stations and Outage Outfitter (updated Oct 19) list it at $899. Outage Authority (Oct 7) said the promo had ended and it was back at $1,199, though Amazon had it at $798.99 that day. Check the current price before buying, and skip it above $1,000.
- Sources: [Outage Outfitter](https://outageoutfitter.com/best/under-1000/), [Compare Power Stations](https://comparepowerstations.com/best/best-under-1000/)

**4. Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, lightest and cheapest 1 kWh ($489)**
- It has 1,070 Wh (about 910 Wh usable) and weighs 23.8 lb.
- The $489 price is at Outbound Power. Jackery's own store raised it to $559.
- Its 400 W solar input is low, and it can't be expanded.
- Source: [Outage Authority review](https://outageauthority.com/reviews/jackery-explorer-1000-v2)

**Also worth a look:** The Anker SOLIX F1500 (1,536 Wh) was listed at $599.99, flagged as an unusually low price, on [Compare Power Stations](https://comparepowerstations.com/best/best-under-1000/). The Bluetti Elite 100 V2 (1,024 Wh, $499) is listed [at Home Depot](https://www.homedepot.com/p/337557774) but currently out of stock.

## Limits to know
- None of these can power a whole house. For 240V loads like a well pump or mini-split, you'd need something like the EcoFlow Delta Pro 3 at $2,799, per Outage Authority.
- The runtime figures are the sites' estimates from manufacturer specs, not independent lab tests. Outage Outfitter says it hasn't tested these units itself.
- Prices change often, so confirm at checkout.

If you tell me what you need to run (fridge, CPAP, sump pump, window AC) and for how long, I can narrow it to one.
